newsitem.title: UK: Siebe shares drop amid "switch" advice.
newsitem.headline: Siebe shares drop amid "switch" advice.

text.p: Shares in Siebe Plc dropped on Friday from Thursday's record peak amid cautious comment following the company's 80 million stg acquistion from General Electric Co Plc, traders said.

Analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett advised investors to switch out of Siebe and into TI Group Plc while the influential Financial Times Lex column said Siebe was trading on a demanding rating and GEC "may be a better bet."
Shares in Siebe were down 11-1/2p at 10.77-1/2 stg by 1004 GMT, after yesterday setting a closing high of 10.89 stg. TI was up 6p at 578-1/2 while GEC was up 3-1/2p 381.

The FT said Siebe had, in the first half of fiscal 1997, missed its target of 10 percent organic sales growth, had limited scope to raise margins and was "heavily exposed to a possible economic slowdown in the U.S."

"None of this detracts from Siebe's quality," the FT said, "but at...a 30 percent premium to the market the group cannot afford to slip up." It said GEC may be a better bet as newly- installed managing director George Simpson starts to sell non-core businesses.
Analysts at Hoare Govett were not immediately available for comment.

On Thursday Siebe said it was expanding its control systems business with the acquisition of Satchwell Controls Ltd from GEC. The stock has doubled since the start of 1995 on the back of strong organic growth and a series of well-received acquisitions.
